As dose increases the user may begin to feel a disconnection from their body

name: ketamine

properties.avoid: Driving, walking, motor activity. Mixing with other depressants such as alcohol, benzodiazepines, and opioids.
properties.dose: Insufflated Threshold: 5-10mg Light: 20-50mg Common: 50-125mg Strong: 125-175mg Heavy: 175-250mg | NOTE: Ketamine is based on weight. These are figures for the average 150 pound male There is no concrete dose for the "K-Hole" as each user is different.
properties.effects: A feeling of drunkenness and well being at low doses. As dose increases the user may begin to feel a disconnection from their body. At 'khole' doses the user may become completely disconnected from both body and mind.
properties.onset: Insufflated: 7.5-20 minutes | Oral: 10-75 minutes | Intramuscular: 2-7.5 minutes | Intravenous: 0-2 minutes
properties.summary: A short-acting dissociative anaesthetic and hallucinogen commonly used in medicine. It is the prototypical dissociative, and is widely used at sub-anesthetic doses recreationally. Small doses are comparable with alcohol, while larger doses are immobilising and lead to psychedelic experiences: the "K-Hole."
